recall.minute: ML is worth using when a problem is intrinsically hard, big, or changing over time; stable, precise rules belong in code. Because ML systems are probabilistic, requirements must be measurable, data-aware and model-aware: they cover data quality and availability, behaviour under uncertainty, and continuous learning. Goals exist at organisational, product, user and model levels, are hierarchical, and can support or conflict, for example accuracy vs latency or cost vs quality. Requirements flow from goals to the decisions people make, to questions those decisions raise, to predictions ML can provide. GR4ML formalises this in a business view (actors, strategic goals, indicators, decision and question goals, insights), an analytics design view (analytics goals, algorithms, softgoals, influences) and a data preparation view (entities, tasks, operators, data flows), illustrated with a credit-risk model retrained monthly on 48 months of data. Measures should relate to goals, be objective and practical, and be accurate and precise.
